questions.question: The first evidence for Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) was based on Francine Shapiro's own experience with eye movements. If she had not been able to consistently repeat, or＿＿＿＿, those effects in other people, one would have to question the reliability of such data. And if her clients' reports of reduced anxiety were not supported by, say, their overt behavior or the reports of their close relatives, one would have to doubt the _______of these data.
questions.reference_answer:
如果Shapiro無法「反覆產生」同樣效果，就要懷疑可靠性。
如果減少焦慮的報告沒有被行為或他人觀察證實，就要懷疑效度。
concepts: 可重複性（replicability）與效度（validity）

questions.question: A professor wants to examine the effects of diet on learning. He places some laboratory rats on a starvation diet (Group A) but eliminates only desserts from the diet of a second group (Group B). During the experiment, the professor discovers that he needs more Group B rats, so he catches some in a local alley. The results of the experiment show that Group B rats are faster at learning a maze, so the professor concludes that diet is related to learning speed. Which statement about his conclusion is most accurate?
options: The professor's conclusion is correct because the number of rats in each group are the same
The professor's conclusion is correct because the two groups of rats were on a different diet
The professor's conclusion is incorrect because the type of rat was a confound
The professor's conclusion is incorrect because the study is correlational
questions.reference_answer: 做法引入了新的變項（老鼠來源、品種、基因、經驗），這就是混淆變項，因為你無法確定是飲食差異還是老鼠來源導致結果。

questions.question: Dr. Wisgoski asks fifty drug addicts a series of questions about their childhoods and then collects blood samples from them. He finds a high correlation between levels of the stress hormone cortisol and the amount of reported childhood trauma. Dr. Wisgoski concludes that childhood trauma causes high levels of stress during adulthood, which, in turn, causes drug addiction. Dr. Wisgoski's operational definition of adult stress level is_____
questions.reference_answer:
Dr. Wisgoski 的成人壓力程度的操作性定義是什麼？
操作性定義 = 用什麼具體可觀測的量來「代表」壓力？
題目說：他收集血液樣本，測量壓力荷爾蒙cortisol的水平。
所以他把「成人壓力」操作性定義為血液中cortisol濃度。

questions.question: Feature detection cannot explain how you can perceive ＿＿＿
options: perceive the same sounds as "I scream" sometimes and "ice cream" at other times
identify a new Honda automobile as a car, even if you had never seen that particular model before
recognize a friend you have not seen in several years
identify a black poodle as a poodle, even if you had previously seen only white poodles
questions.reference_answer:
Feature detection 只能解釋「特徵模式辨識」，無法解釋語境對知覺的影響。
題目中：
 「I scream」和「ice cream」是同樣的聲音，但因語境不同而知覺不同，這超出了純特徵偵測理論能解釋的範疇。
concepts: 知覺解釋的高層次處理：特徵偵測理論（feature detection theory）

questions.question: Participants in an experiment are asked to look at pictures of driving scenes taken From the driver's point of view. When the scenes are changed, participants' cars easily detect some small changes, such as wording on a traffic sign. However, they often miss large irrelevant changes such as a disappearing building. This is because of＿＿＿＿
questions.reference_answer:
即使有大變化（像建築物消失），只要不在注意焦點，人們也不會察覺。
這正是inattentional blindness（不注意盲視）：當注意力集中在某些特定事物時，對其他明顯變化完全無感。
concepts: 選擇性注意（selective attention）、改變錯覺（change blindness）與不注意盲視（inattentional blindness）
questions.key_concepts: 選擇性注意（selective attention）、改變錯覺（change blindness）與不注意盲視（inattentional blindness）

questions.question: Your friend is ordering pizza and wants to know which toppings you want. You say pepperoni, sausage, green pepper, olives, mushrooms, onions, tomatoes and pineapple.” Your friend doesn’t write this down but then dials the pizza place and places order. Which topping is your friend most likely to forget?
questions.reference_answer:
系列位置效應（serial position effect）：
首因效應：最先講的容易記住（如pepperoni, sausage）
近因效應：最後講的也容易記住（pineapple）
中間的資訊最容易被忘掉。
題目問：
 朋友沒寫下來，最可能忘記哪個？
 → 中間提到的項目。
concepts: 短期記憶與系列位置效果（primacy & recency effect）

questions.question: Dolly is conducting a study in which she asks basketball players from several colleges to recall their win-loss outcomes of certain games in the past season. She finds that some players incorrectly remember game outcomes, even when they are considered important games. This example highlights that_____
options: recall is susceptible to interference from short-term memory
the feeling-of-knowing phenomenon also affects long-term retrieval
long-term memories are subject to major errors and distortion
only flashbulb memories tend to retain their accuracy in long-term memory
questions.reference_answer:
長期記憶的錯誤與扭曲：即使是重要事件（比賽結果），人們也會記錯。
關鍵概念：
長期記憶不是完全準確，經常會有錯誤或扭曲。
concepts: 記憶的重構性與扭曲（memory distortion）

questions.question: Jamie has had her hippocampus removed. She can't form new memories but improves at tennis. Her skill will ____.
options: decrease unless she stops taking lessons
questions.reference_answer:
內隱記憶 vs. 外顯記憶：
海馬迴（hippocampus）損傷 → 無法形成新外顯記憶（記不起自己練習過）。
但程序性記憶（技能學習）仍保留 → 技術仍會進步。
因此她的網球技巧會持續進步。
concepts: 程序性記憶（Procedural Memory）與海馬迴（hippocampus）無關

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true regarding language acquisition?
options: Humans must acquire language during a critical period to acquire complex features of their language
Balanced bilinguals show greater cognitive flexibility than those who speak one language
Nonhuman primates can use language as well as children
Children learn syntax through both modeling and biological preparedness
questions.reference_answer:
語言習得的事實：
✅ a. 有臨界期→正確
✅ b. 雙語者認知彈性較高→正確
✅ d. 小孩透過模仿與生物預備學語法→正確
❌ c. 非人靈長類無法像兒童一樣熟練地掌握語言，特別是複雜語法結構，這是錯的

questions.question: A picture of a Coke bottle is flashed on a computer monitor, but too briefly for a viewer to notice. According to the concept of priming, which result is most likely?
options: There will be no effect because the viewer is unaware of the event
The viewer will recognize related words (e.g., diet, Pepsi) more quickly than unrelated words (e.g., computer, pencil) on a test a few seconds later
There will be faster recognition of related words if the viewer is in an altered state of consciousness

questions.question: Nam has been learning to reduce his test anxiety by using cognitive restructuring. Which thought would be an example of a successful application of his therapy?

"All I want is to do the best job that I can on this test."
"I will talk to my friends about my problems more often, instead of keeping them bottled up inside."
questions.reference_answer:
認知重建（cognitive restructuring）是認知行為治療（CBT）核心技巧,辨識並修正導致焦慮的不適應思考模式（如全有全無、災難化、過度概化）,替換成更平衡實際的想法。

(B) 時間管理屬「行為策略」,不是認知層次的介入
(C) ✓ 把「我必須考完美」這類焦慮製造型思考重建為「盡力就好」的合理目標,典型的認知重建成果
(D) 尋求社會支持屬人際／情緒因應,不是認知重建

關鍵辨識:認知重建必須動到「思考內容本身」,不是改變行為（B）或情緒處理方式（D）。

questions.question: Your new housemate comes home from on-campus registration, throws his coat angrily on the floor; goes to his room, and slams the door without greeting you. You conclude that your housemate is a hostile, unfriendly person. Your conclusion is the result of _____.
questions.reference_answer:
忽略了他可能只是當天心情不好或壓力大，直接把行為歸因為人格特質（「他就是不友善的人」）。
✅ 這正是基本歸因錯誤 (fundamental attribution error)。

questions.question: If everything else is equal, which factor would least affect how attracted you are to someone?
options: The person wears nicer clothes than you normally wear
The person is about as physically attractive as you are
The person rides the same bus as you do every morning
The person shares your taste in music and political views
questions.reference_answer:
吸引力的經典因素：
親近性（proximity） → 常搭同一班公車（c）
相似性（similarity） → 有相同興趣看法（d）
匹配假說（matching hypothesis） → 吸引力相近（b）
❌ 穿著比你好看（a）對吸引力影響最小，通常不是主要決定因素。

questions.question: What is an important assumption in the field of neuropsychology?
options: Different psychological processes are controlled by the same few brain regions
Behavior is motivated primarily by biological sources
Complicated mental tasks involve subtasks that can be studied separately
Only healthy, fully functioning brains can provide insight into psychological processes
questions.reference_answer:
神經心理學的重要假設：
✅ 複雜的心理功能可以拆解成較簡單的子過程，分別研究，例如記憶可分為編碼、儲存、提取等階段。
